# Step 2.65: correcting a tracked game in the grid

## Layer 1 (builder one): below the screen

What exists, in `packages/core/src/modules/games` (all exported from its `index.ts`):

- `apply-plays.ts`, `applyPlays(...)`: the one door. The body of `games.apply_tracker_commands` that applies commands with the engine and saves events, state, lines and score, moved out unchanged; the tracker's batches and the grid both go through it.
- `grid-correction-plays.ts`, `gridCorrectionPlays(teams, replayedLines, wantedLines)`: pure. Gives `{ ok: true, plays }` (take-backs first, then fouls and turnovers, then baskets) or `{ ok: false, problems }` (`team-not-in-game`, `player-listed-twice`, `basket-taken-back`).
- `commands/read-tracked-box-score.ts`, `readTrackedBoxScore({ gameId })`, permission `games.correct`: `{ gameId, sequence, correctable, notCorrectable?, lines: TrackedGridRow[] }`, a row per player of the game's day (`teamId, personId, jerseyNumber, secondsPlayed, points, fg1, fg2, fg3, fouls, turnovers`).
- `commands/correct-tracked-box-score.ts`, `correctTrackedBoxScore({ gameId, sequence, lines })`, permission `games.correct`; a line is `trackedGridLine`: `teamId, personId` and any of `fg1, fg2, fg3, fouls, turnovers` (left out stays). Gives `{ sequence, plays }`. Refusals (`CorrectTrackedBoxScoreError`): `game-not-found`, `not-allowed`, `not-tracked`, `game-final` (reopen first), `game-not-live`, `reason-needed` (live but not reopened), `changed-since-read` (pass the read's `sequence`), `team-not-in-game`, `player-listed-twice`, `player-not-on-team`, `statistic-not-kept`, `rule` with `problem: 'basket-taken-back'` or `problem: 'engine'` (the engine's own words).
- Registered in `packages/core/src/commands.ts`; activity words `activity.games.correct_tracked_box_score` and `activityNamed...` in `packages/site/src/messages/en/activity.ts`; the read listed in `apps/web/src/server/activity-messages.test.ts`; two rows each in `role-matrix.test.ts`; isolation cases in `packages/database/src/isolation/grid-correction-cases.test-helper.ts`. Decision T-405 (pending file), spec T6 §8 corrected. No migration.

Run and passed: games folder of core (530, before the read test), `grid-correction-plays.test.ts` (5), `read-tracked-box-score.test.ts` (2), `correct-tracked-box-score.test.ts` (5: the foul moved is `unfoul` then `foul` in the log and the replay gives the grid), role matrix with activity messages (272), isolation folder (389), `tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs`, typecheck, `npm run check`. Broken by hand once each: the order of plays (2 failed), the `changed-since-read` check together with the side of a team (3 failed), the open-reopen check of the read (1 failed).

What is left. Layer 2: the screen in `apps/web/src/app/[league]/admin/games` (an "Edit box score" for a tracked game, reading `readTrackedBoxScore`, offered only when `correctable`, otherwise a link to reopen; the save sends `sequence` back; words for every refusal in a message file). Layer 3: the browser test and the pinned lists (page-step rows, harmful-text test, `nothing-unfinished`).

What I distrust:

- A basket cannot be lowered or moved (T-405): the engine has no take-back of an earlier basket. If the founder wants it, `packages/sports` needs an "unscore" command, which the build plan does not allow yet.
- The admin's plays bump the game's events while a scorekeeper's device may still hold the session; that device learns of them only on its next refusal or reload (T-113).
- `isolation` and the matrix only cover a save with no lines; the writes themselves are covered in core's memory stores, not against PostgreSQL.

## Review (independent reviewer)

Item 1, the move (b47315c7): faithful. The body lines of `apply-plays.ts` are the old ones word for word (compared with `git show` and `diff`); ids, the duplicate check, the lock, `seq`, the refusals and the one transaction stay in `apply-tracker-commands.ts`, and `seq = applied.seq` comes before the answer is written down, as before. Passed: core games folder (532), the database tracker files (`tracker-commands`, `tracked-game-end-commands`, `table-players-commands`, `scorekeeper-reopen-commands`: 30), browser `tracker-offline-test` (17) and `tracked-grid-test` (27) in one chunk.

Item 2, attacks (a throwaway test, not committed): stale `sequence` and the same save posted twice (second `changed-since-read`, no plays added twice), ended and not reopened, or ended again on the tablet after the reopen (`game-final`), a scorekeeper (`not-allowed`), -1, 1.5 and 1000 (`invalid-input`), the other team's player, an unknown person, another game's team (refused by name): all refused, nothing written. A 12-play save: the replayed log gives exactly the saved state (`derive` equal: lines, team fouls, bonus, minutes unchanged). Item 3: the owner can end the game again (on the scoring screen, End game); the public page then reads Final, Corrected, with the grid's lines, and standings answer (not compared before and after).

- Medium. A scorekeeper's Undo on the scoring screen walks back into the admin's correction: after a grid save, a tablet tap and two Undos, the second Undo took back the admin's foul (tablet `undo` after `correct-tracked-box-score`, as in the throwaway test). Nothing stops or tells it; the log still explains it, but the correction is silently half undone, and the end of a correction happens on that very screen. Name it on the scoring screen, or decide (T-405) that Undo stops at a correction.
- Medium. What the admin must do today to finish: save the grid, tap "Open the scoring screen", open the game there (taking it from any device that holds it), tap End game. The grid page has no "end it again", and a corrected game left live is out of the standings until someone does this. The words (`admin-games.ts` line 15) say so; a button on the grid page, or an end in the same save, would close the gap.
- Low. Every grid play lands in the period and clock time the game ended in (`correct-tracked-box-score.ts` line 159, `at: now`; the engine takes the current period): a foul moved from period 1 counts toward the last period's team fouls and bonus (7 period fouls, penalty, in the test), and the public play by play shows the corrected plays at the last period's time.
- Low, test gap. The check of a statistic the season does not keep before anything is written (`correct-tracked-box-score.ts` lines 140 to 143) is tested by nothing: broken by hand, the 11 tests of `correct-tracked-box-score.test.ts` and `tracked-grid.test.ts` still passed; without it a direct call with turnovers in a standard season throws (a server error) instead of `statistic-not-kept`. Restored.
- Low. A grid save has no limit on plays: 200 lines with 999 in each box is one transaction of up to a million events; a typo (30 for 3) adds 27 baskets that only Undo on the scoring screen takes back, one by one, from the newest.

Item 4: no wait without a limit, no check passing on a timeout or behind a `.catch` in the lane's tests (the device loop in `tracked-grid-test.mjs` near line 361 has a limit and a check after it). No migration is needed.

## Fix round (fix helper)

What is fixed (items 1 and 3 of the lead's decisions; item 2 is left, below):

- Item 1, "End the game again" (T-407, pending; spec T6 §8 corrected): the game's admin page and the grid of a reopened tracked game offer it to whoever may correct the game (`end-again-form.tsx`, `endTrackedGameAgainAction` in `actions.ts`, `runEndAgainAction` in `run-tracked-grid-action.ts`). It is `games.correct_tracked_box_score` with `end: true` and no lines: the scoring screen's own `{ type: 'end' }` tap through `applyPlays`, so no second way to end a game and no device taken over. A level score the rules do not allow is refused (`tie-not-allowed`, words beside the button). It lands on the game's page, now final, which says "Saved" with the score. `admin.boxScore.done.reopenTracked` now names the button.
- Item 3: `statistic-not-kept` is now tested; one save writes at most `maxCorrectionPlays` (200) plays, else `too-many-plays`, said at the top of the grid (`admin.boxScore.tracked.refused.too-many-plays`). No new command or read, so no role-matrix or isolation row. No migration.

Run and passed: `correct-tracked-box-score.test.ts` (8: end again while the tablet holds the game, then its tap refused; level score refused, nothing written; not-kept and too many plays refused, nothing written), core games folder (535), `tracked-grid.test.ts` (7: too many plays at the top; end again, stale refused, then final), games-area and `packages/site` (172), `npm run test:web` (290), `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`, `tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs` (11); browser `tracked-grid-test` (35) with `games-area-test` (38), then `tracker-offline-test` (17).

`tracked-grid-test` now: the owner ends the game from the grid while a scorekeeper's device holds it; the game's page says final; every play is kept; the device's next tap is told "This game cannot be scored now: it is over, cancelled or postponed." and saves nothing; the public page has the grid's lines, Final and "Corrected on"; the standings differ from while it was live. Reopened and ended again from the game's own page with no change: the standings are the same text. Reopened, an away player given three 3-pointers (away wins 9 to 8) and ended again: the standings change.

Broken by hand once each: the not-kept check (1 failed), the play limit (1 failed), the tie check (1 failed), the end left out of the plays (1 failed), the web's limit mapping (1 failed), `end: true` left out of the page's command (unit: 1 failed; `tracked-grid-test`: 3 failed).

What is left:

- Item 2 (a scorekeeper's Undo walking back into a correction) did not fit the budget. Nothing the stored event carries tells a grid play from a tablet's: its account can be an admin who also scores, and events keep no session or source. It needs a field (a source, or the ids of a correction's plays read with the tracker's state) and a few lines in `apps/web/src/features/tracker`; a decision number (T-408) is free for it.
- Item 4 is the lead's polish list.

What I distrust:

- "Loses nothing it typed" is checked as the server keeping every play and the refused tap saving nothing; the device's own list of refused taps was not read.
- The standings are compared as the whole page's text, so they prove a change, not which row changed.

## Third fix helper

Cause found (T-409, pending): the TEST, not the product. The failed run (`.local/grid.log`) had one problem only, the count after the wait: `told.first().waitFor` had seen the words, then `told.count()` found none. By design the device shows "This game cannot be scored now" only until `lost()` has loaded the game as the server has it; then `showsFinalPanel` puts the final panel in its place (`tracker-notice.ts`). The tap was refused and saved nothing in that run too (that check passed), and `lost()` lists the tap as not saved, so no tap is accepted or lost.

What changed in `tracked-grid-test`:

- The words are watched for as they are drawn (a text watcher set up on the device before its tap), then waited for with `tapLimit`; after them the device's final panel (`[data-final]`) is waited for and checked. Nothing it checked before is checked less.
- The step that changes the winner now checks the public page says Final and "Corrected on" (S-81: the result changed). Searched S-81 in `DECISIONS.md` and P7: a correction that leaves the result as first final is rightly not marked, so the earlier step's "not Corrected" stands.
- New `packages/database/src/queries/list-game-events-after.test.ts` (PGlite): the mark comes back through `payload jsonb` as `source: "correction"`; an event without it, or with an unknown value, reads with no `source`.

Run: `tracked-grid-test` twice before the change (passed, 39) and once after (passed, 40), so three passes in a row, the last with the fix; the new database test (1); `node scripts/fence-filter-check.mjs list-game-events-after` (1 filter caught, 0 problems); `tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs`; `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`.

Broken by hand once each: the notice left out for `game-not-live` in `tracker-notice.ts` (`tracked-grid-test`: the watch timed out, 3 problems), restored; the query reading another key than `playSourceKey` (database test: 1 failed), restored.

Confirming look (read only):

- An older tracker (no `X-Tracker-Changes`): `tracker-state-endpoint.ts` leaves out `changes` and `corrections` then, but `tracker-state-endpoint.test.ts` pins neither: nothing proves the old answer's shape. Left: a test with a correction in the stand-in world.
- Undo twice fast: `useUndoAsk` reads the controller's game at the tap (`controller.status().game`), not the last drawing, and Undo has its tap rest (`takeBackRestMs`), so a second fast tap is asked about or ignored. No test taps twice fast.
- "End the game again" by a scorekeeper: refused by the command's `games.correct` gate before the `end` branch; the role matrix row has no `end: true`, and the core test of refusals sends lines, not an end. A coach: no coach in core's memory fixture nor in the role matrix (team scopes), so neither is tested for an end. Left: both.

What I distrust: the watcher reads text nodes of the whole page on every change; it is set up only for this tap.

## Last helper

Merge of `build/stage-1` (2.155 part 3, 2.69): no conflicts in the text. Both lanes' behaviour kept, and where they meet:

- While Undo's question is asked, the mercy notice waits in its own place in the pad, hidden and out of reach (`.court-waits`: `display: contents; visibility: hidden`), so nothing moves and the hint does not come back in its place; its answers rest again when it comes back, so the tap that closed the question cannot land on one. The question is a sheet over the screen and moves nothing.
- A fast double Undo asked, then the second tap landed on the question's scrim and closed it. Now the question's answers (and the scrim) rest from the tap that asked (`undoAsked` in the screen's resting places), and a tap Undo would not take (its own rest) asks nothing.
